971class Device: 

972 """Represent a GPU and act as an entry point for cuda.core features. 

973  

974 This is a singleton object that helps ensure interoperability 

975 across multiple libraries imported in the process to both see 

976 and use the same GPU device. 

977  

978 While acting as the entry point, many other CUDA resources can be 

979 allocated such as streams and buffers. Any :obj:`~_context.Context` dependent 

980 resource created through this device, will continue to refer to 

981 this device's context. 

982  

983 Newly returned :obj:`~_device.Device` objects are thread-local singletons 

984 for a specified device. 

985  

986 A pickled :obj:`~_device.Device` names its device by UUID. Unpickling 

987 returns the device with that UUID in the receiving process, whatever its 

988 ordinal is there, and raises ``RuntimeError`` if that device is not 

989 visible. The pickled form is for processes on the same machine. 

990  

991 Note 

992 ---- 

993 Will not initialize the GPU. 

994  

995 Parameters 

996 ---------- 

997 device_id : int, optional 

998 Device ordinal to return a :obj:`~_device.Device` object for. 

999 Default value of `None` return the currently used device. 

1000  

1001 """ 

1002 __slots__ = ( 

1003 "_device_id", 

1004 "_memory_resource", 

1005 "_has_inited", 

1006 "_properties", 

1007 "_resources", 

1008 "_uuid", 

1009 "_context", 

1010 "__weakref__", 

1011 )

1253 def set_current(self, Context ctx: Context | None = None) -> Context | None: 

1254 """Set device to be used for GPU executions. 

1255  

1256 Initializes CUDA and sets the calling thread to a valid CUDA 

1257 context. By default the primary context is used, but optional `ctx` 

1258 parameter can be used to explicitly supply a :obj:`~_context.Context` object. 

1259  

1260 Providing a `ctx` causes the previous set context to be popped and returned. 

1261  

1262 If `ctx` was created on a different device than this receiver, the call 

1263 is delegated to that device's own :meth:`set_current`. This keeps the 

1264 owning device's bookkeeping consistent and lets a context this method 

1265 handed out for a foreign device be pushed back through any ``Device`` 

1266 object, matching the CUDA context stack's own thread-wide semantics. 

1267  

1268 Parameters 

1269 ---------- 

1270 ctx : :obj:`~_context.Context`, optional 

1271 Optional context to push onto this device's current thread stack. 

1272  

1273 Returns 

1274 ------- 

1275 :obj:`~_context.Context`, optional 

1276 The previous context, or ``None`` if no context was current. When 

1277 returned, its ``device_id`` identifies the device that was 

1278 previously current. 

1279  

1280 Examples 

1281 -------- 

1282 Acts as an entry point of this object. Users always start a code by 

1283 calling this method, e.g. 

1284  

1285 >>> from cuda.core import Device 

1286 >>> dev0 = Device(0) 

1287 >>> dev0.set_current() 

1288 >>> # ... do work on device 0 ... 

1289

1297 Context_check_open(ctx) 2c iMoM=EpM`HqMrM`k

1298 if ctx._device_id != self._device_id: 2c iMoM=EpM`HqM`k

1299 # The CUDA context stack is per-thread, not per-Device-object, 

1300 # so pushing/popping a foreign-device context is delegated to 

1301 # the device that owns it; its own bookkeeping (_context, 

1302 # _has_inited) is what should track this push, not ours. 

1303 return Device(ctx._device_id).set_current(ctx) 

1304 if self._has_inited and self._context is not None: 2c iMoM=EpM`HqM`k

1312 # cuCtxSetCurrent replaces the top of the thread's context stack 

1313 # in one driver call (or binds ctx when nothing is current), so 

1314 # a failure leaves the previous context current instead of 

1315 # leaving the thread with no context, as a failed pop-then-push 

1316 # would. 

1317 HANDLE_RETURN(cydriver.cuCtxSetCurrent(curr_ctx)) 2c iMoM=EpM`HqM`k
